answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond before it can influence a market, then slash that bond when its actions are proven fraudulent through a public challenge process. The bond is tied to an account’s economic stake, not its claimed name, so splitting one attacker into many onyx, sable, or glacier identities does not create free influence: each identity needs its own locked capital. The attacker pays in capital tied up, fees, and losses on any exposed account.
